newsitem.title: INDIA: India Punjab cotton regains initiative, low stocks.
newsitem.headline: India Punjab cotton regains initiative, low stocks.

text.p: Indian Punjab cotton prices on Monday bounced back from reduced levels while Gujarat cotton was steady, dealers said.
Punjab cotton rose on a shortage of ready stock due to the tail-end of the season as arrivals dropped to negligible levels.

In spot deals, Punjab saw-ginned rose by 20 rupees to 1,825/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees to 1,030/1,070 rupees per maund. Cotton F-414 rose by 10 rupees to 2,060/2,090 rupees per maund.
"Fresh mill buying also helped prices to bounce back," a broker said.
Gujarat cotton was steady amidst limited activity. In spot deals, Gujarat Kalyan was quiet at 13,900/14,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton was steady at 12,700 rupees per candy.
